title: The Imperative to “Show” Rather than “Tell”
use_cases: Use when prioritizing demonstrative details over straightforward exposition
Implement when illustrating character emotions through physical behaviors
Configure when anchoring emotional states in tangible, observable actions
Use when seeking to mirror the cinematic process of visual and auditory storytelling
content:
One of the core tenets of cinematic writing is the prioritisation of demonstrative, evocative details over straightforward exposition. For instance, rather than stating that a character experiences trepidation, illustrate this emotion through their physical responses and observable behaviours:

Telling: The protagonist was consumed by fear.

Showing: The protagonist’s hands trembled as they reached for the doorknob, their breath quickening with each step closer.

By anchoring emotional states in tangible, observable actions, writers allow readers to infer meaning and engage with the narrative on a more intuitive level. The act of interpreting these cues mirrors the process of watching a film, where visual and auditory signals convey depth and nuance.
